evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that all products that read and/or transmit NMEA 2000 information must be certified by NMEA, that the NMEA 2000 standard is a registered trademark, that certification is based on the NMEA 2000 License Agreement and produces a mandatory encrypted certification file that NMEA validates before certification is granted, and that use of the official NMEA 2000 logo and the term 'NMEA 2000 Certified' follows validation.
evidence.limitations: Association webpage summary, not the licensed standard text; no fee schedule for NMEA 2000 licensing was printed on the page. Applies to entities that implement NMEA 2000; MAREA implements none.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that each manufacturer must purchase a NMEA 2000 Manufacturer code issued by NMEA and that manufacturer code assignments take up to 60 days, and that a unique NMEA 2000 Product code must be purchased for each certified product.
evidence.limitations: No fee amount is printed on the page; lead time is stated as 'up to 60 days' by the association and is not a contractual availability commitment to MAREA.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that the NMEA 0183 Interface Standard is a copyrighted document available only from NMEA, defines a 4800-baud serial data bus with one talker and multiple listeners, is not sold through an online store, and lists prices of USD 1,150 (NMEA manufacturer member), USD 7,500 (government/industrial/testing) and USD 10,000 (consumer electronics); latest version is 4.30 and NMEA 0183-HS defines 38.4 kbaud.
evidence.limitations: Prices are the published USD price list for the standard document, not a MAREA quotation; no purchase was made and no member discount was confirmed as available to MAREA.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that an NMEA 0183 Manufacturer Mnemonic Code carries an administrative fee of USD 200, requires purchase of the standard at the applicable industry-group price, and is issued to companies only, not individuals.
evidence.limitations: Association webpage statement; no application was filed in MC-11.

It does not enumerate Annex III 'important' product classes or the exact scope test, so downstream classification of a MAREA product as default/important/critical is NOT established by this source. Page last-update stamp displayed: 7 September 2026.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: The CRA applies to products with digital elements placed on the EU market, regardless of where the manufacturer is based, that can connect directly or indirectly to other devices or networks, covering both hardware (IoT devices, industrial control systems, microchips) and software products (apps, computer programmes). Some products are classified 'important' or 'critical' and are subject to stricter conformity assessment; Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392 sets out the technical descriptions of those categories. The CRA excludes certain products, including medical devices under specific EU regulations, aviation and automotive products under sector-specific legislation, and marine equipment within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU. Manufacturers must perform a risk assessment, apply secure-by-default configuration and access control, provide security updates during the support period, provide documentation and a declaration of conformity, and report severe incidents and actively exploited vulnerabilities. Importers must verify manufacturer compliance; distributors must ensure CE marking and user information. Fines can reach 2.5 % of global annual turnover.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary. The page's 'FROM WHEN DOES THE REGULATION APPLY' dates were not rendered in the retrieved copy, so no CRA date is taken from this record (dates are taken from EVD-MC11-301 and EVD-MC11-303). The exclusion for 'marine equipment within the scope of Directive 2014/90/EU' is narrow: it does not cover recreational-craft electronics that are outside the MED scope (see EVD-MC11-311).

evidence.publisher: European Commission — Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology
evidence.supportedAssertion: As of 11 September 2026 manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents affecting the security of products with digital elements (Article 71(2) CRA); open-source software stewards are subject to the reporting obligation of Article 24(3) from 11 December 2027. Reporting is through the CRA Single Reporting Platform established by ENISA under Article 16, operational as of 11 September 2026: an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware, a full notification within 72 hours, a final report no later than 14 days after a corrective measure is available (actively exploited vulnerabilities) or within one month of the 72-hour notification (severe incidents). Notifications go to the CSIRT of the main establishment and simultaneously to ENISA, and are shared with other CSIRTs. A delegated act on CSIRT withholding of notifications was adopted on 11 December 2025.
evidence.limitations: Commission guidance page, not the legal text. It describes obligations that attach to a manufacturer placing a product with digital elements on the market; MAREA places none today, so the obligations are prospective and not yet triggered.

evidence.publisher: European Commission — Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs
evidence.supportedAssertion: Radio Equipment Directive 2014/53/EU establishes a framework for placing radio equipment on the market with essential requirements for safety and health, electromagnetic compatibility and efficient use of the radio spectrum, plus additional aspects including protection of privacy and personal data, protection against fraud, interoperability, access to emergency services and the combination of radio equipment with software. It was published in the OJEU on 22 May 2014, entered into force on 11 June 2014 and applies as of 13 June 2016, with a transitional period that ended on 12 June 2017 (Article 48). Article 45 establishes the TCAM committee. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1354 Article 10(10) defines a pictogram for printed product documentation. The Commission adopted Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 of 29 October 2021 activating Articles 3(3)(d), (e) and (f) for certain categories of radio equipment; to avoid overlap with the CRA the Commission adopted a repealing Delegated Regulation on 16 February 2026 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/339 repealing Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 was published in the Official Journal on 29 April 2026, with repeal effective 11 December 2027. The initiative on Articles 3(3)(i) and 4 (reconfigurable radio systems) was abandoned by the Commission on 20 January 2026. Voluntary/unregulated certificates are not a recognised means to prove compliance; CE marking may only be affixed after testing and the prescribed conformity assessment.
evidence.limitations: Commission policy page. It states the essential-requirement structure but does not reproduce the article text of Article 3 or the conformity-assessment modules; those are taken from the Portuguese transposition in EVD-MC11-317, which is national law implementing the same directive and is flagged as such.

evidence.publisher: European Commission — Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs
evidence.supportedAssertion: Affixing CE marking is a six-step manufacturer process: identify the applicable directive(s)/regulation(s) and harmonised standards; verify product-specific requirements; identify whether an independent conformity assessment by a notified body is necessary (NANDO database); test the product and check conformity; draw up the EU declaration of conformity under the manufacturer's sole responsibility, including manufacturer details, essential characteristics and, where applicable, the notified body identification number and a legally binding signature; and draw up and keep the technical documentation, which must be established before submission to a notified body or at the latest when placing the first device on the market and kept for the period specified in the applicable act. The CE marking must be affixed visibly and legibly on the product or, if not possible, on the packaging and accompanying documents, with components of the same vertical dimension not smaller than 5 mm; where a notified body was involved its identification number must also be displayed; CE marking must not be affixed to products outside the scope of a CE-marking act.
evidence.limitations: Horizontal Commission guidance; it does not determine which acts apply to a given MAREA configuration — that is the object of D23 and remains subject to qualified review.

evidence.publisher: European Commission — Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs
evidence.supportedAssertion: Low Voltage Directive 2014/35/EU covers health and safety risks of electrical equipment operating with an input or output voltage between 50 and 1000 V alternating current and between 75 and 1500 V direct current, and has been applicable since 20 April 2016. The directive does not require notified bodies to assess products; the manufacturer alone is responsible for determining compliance through the conformity assessment procedures. The page records that the (former) general product safety directive covers consumer goods below those voltage thresholds.
evidence.limitations: Commission policy page. Voltage thresholds are stated for input OR output voltage, which matters for a bundled mains power supply; the page does not analyse 12 V DC marine systems, so the non-applicability reasoning in D23 is an engineering/legal reading flagged for qualified review.

evidence.publisher: European Commission — Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs
evidence.supportedAssertion: Electromagnetic Compatibility Directive 2014/30/EU was published in the Official Journal L 96/79 of 29 March 2014 and repealed Directive 2004/108/EC as from 20 April 2016. It limits electromagnetic emissions from equipment so that, when used as intended, it does not disturb radio and telecommunication and other equipment, and governs immunity. It applies to equipment (apparatus and fixed installations) when placed on the market and/or taken into service, and requires good engineering practice for fixed installations. Harmonised standards must be referenced in the OJEU to give presumption of conformity; notified bodies are listed in NANDO.
evidence.limitations: Commission policy page. It does not reproduce Article 2 (scope exclusions), so the exclusion of radio equipment covered by the RED is evidenced instead through the Portuguese transposition (EVD-MC11-317, Article 2(2)) and through the RED's own EMC essential requirement (EVD-MC11-304).

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (General Product Safety Regulation) applies to products made available on the EU market that are not covered by other specific EU product safety legislation, and to risks and aspects not already covered by such legislation; it applies to new, used, repaired or reconditioned products and to all sales channels including distance selling. It sets a general safety requirement assessed against product characteristics, effect on other products, labelling and warnings, categories of consumers and the product's cybersecurity features and evolving/learning functionalities. It requires a responsible economic operator in the EU for each product (EU manufacturer, importer, authorised representative or fulfilment service provider); manufacturers must ensure safety by design, carry out internal risk analyses and technical documentation, inform consumers and authorities through the Safety Business Gateway, provide product safety and traceability information, keep a complaints register, provide product information on request for 10 years and supply-chain traceability for 6 years, and run recalls with a mandatory recall notice template and at least two remedies. Importers and distributors have verification and escalation duties.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary. The application date was not rendered in the retrieved copy; the 13 December 2024 application date recorded in D23 is flagged as requiring qualified confirmation. The regulation does not require CE marking.

evidence.supportedAssertion: The EU batteries framework is governed by Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, which establishes harmonised rules for all batteries placed on the EU market regardless of origin, composition or whether sold separately or incorporated into products, and covers five categories: portable batteries, light means of transport (LMT) batteries, electric vehicle batteries, industrial batteries and starting/lighting/ignition batteries. It sets binding requirements for sustainability, safety, labelling, supply-chain due diligence and end-of-life management. The regulation has been in force since 17 August 2023 and applies from 18 February 2024.
evidence.limitations: Commission policy overview. It does not enumerate every producer obligation or the appliance-removability provision; that detail comes from EVD-MC11-310.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 covers portable, LMT, EV, industrial and SLI batteries and sets lifecycle rules including waste collection targets for producers of portable batteries (63 % by end-2027, 73 % by end-2030), lithium/cobalt/copper/lead/nickel recovery targets, recycled-content minima, recycling-efficiency targets, a requirement that portable batteries incorporated into appliances be removable and replaceable by the end user by 2027, restrictions on hazardous substances, carbon-footprint information, labelling requirements applying from 2026 with a QR code from 2027, and battery passports for LMT/industrial/EV batteries. It amends Directive 2008/98/EC and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and repeals Directive 2006/66/EC.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary; the precise application dates were not rendered in the retrieved copy (the 18 February 2024 date is taken from EVD-MC11-309). The summary does not distinguish producer-registration mechanics per Member State.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: Marine Equipment Directive 2014/90/EU applies to equipment on ships flying an EU flag (whether or not the vessel was in the EU when the equipment was fitted), implements international maritime safety conventions for equipment on those ships, requires assessment by an independent third party (notified body), and requires the certification mark ('wheel mark') where the equipment meets the requirements. Equipment manufacturers may attach an electronic tag (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/414, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2018/608). Member States must carry out market surveillance and suppliers must withdraw non-compliant or risky equipment. The Commission adopts annual implementing acts on design, construction, performance requirements and testing standards.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary. It does not list the equipment items in scope (those are in the annual implementing act), so MED non-applicability for recreational-craft electronics is a reasoned determination (D23) requiring qualified review, not a proof.

evidence.publisher: Ministerio de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible — Dirección General de la Marina Mercante (Spain)
evidence.supportedAssertion: Spanish marine equipment homologation (homologación) is governed by Real Decreto 1837/2000 of 10 November 2000 (BOE 28-11-2000), Título II, Capítulo VII (inspection and certification of civil vessels); Real Decreto 701/2016 of 23 December 2016, which regulates the requirements for marine equipment intended to be installed on board ships and transposes Directive 2014/90/EU; and Orden FOM/2258/2015 of 23 October 2015, Annex A.1, which lists the marine equipment subject to it. Conformity is assessed under Real Decreto 701/2016 Annex II using modules B (EC type-examination by a notified body), D, E, F, G and H (notified-body quality-assurance or verification modules), with wheel-mark CE marking and the notified body's identification number, and the notified-body group database is at mared.org.
evidence.limitations: Spanish administration guidance page. It establishes the national homologation architecture and the equipment-subject list reference (Orden FOM/2258/2015 Anexo A.1) but the Anexo A.1 item list was NOT retrieved this session, so whether any MAREA item appears on it is unverified.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU restricts the use of hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment; an annex sets the covered EEE categories from household appliances to IT equipment plus an open catch-all category relevant from July 2019; the ban applies to all EEE and to cables and spare parts; a short list of exclusions covers weapons, space equipment, large-scale stationary industrial tools, fixed installations and photovoltaic panels. Manufacturers must design and produce EEE in line with the requirements, importers must check equipment, and distributors must ensure the standards are met. Directive (EU) 2017/2102 amended it (excluding pipe organs and some non-road mobile machinery; removing the ban on secondary-market operations) and exemption lists are continuously updated.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary; it does not give the substance-concentration limits (RoHS Annex II) or the CE-marking/marking article references.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU recasts Directive 2002/96/EC and does not apply to certain EEE, notably material for military or space purposes, filament bulbs, active implantable medical devices and means of transport. Member States must set up a register of all companies producing or importing EEE, allow free return of WEEE, apply a minimum collection rate (45 % from 2016, 65 % from 2019), license treatment plants and require producers to meet treatment targets and finance collection, treatment, recovery and disposal. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/290 sets the format for registration and reporting of EEE producers. Amending Directive (EU) 2024/884 clarifies producer responsibility for costs following a Court of Justice judgment and introduces a review clause for the Commission by end-2026.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary; the summary's transposition deadlines were not rendered in the retrieved copy. National producer-registration mechanics are Member-State law and were not verified for Spain or Portugal in this session.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: Directive 2013/53/EU (recreational craft and personal watercraft) lays down requirements for manufacturers, importers and distributors of watercraft, specifies design categories A–D, and makes all watercraft, designated components and propulsion engines subject to CE marking, affixed on the craft builder's plate (watercraft) or directly on the engine (propulsion engines). Other essential requirements include a watercraft identification number, builder's plate, falling-overboard/reboarding provisions, visibility, a written manual, structure/stability/buoyancy by design category, and an emergency stopping device for tiller-controlled outboard engines. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1 clarifies watercraft identification, and implementing decisions publish the harmonised standards list.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary. The summary does not list the 'designated components' (Annex II of the directive), so the exclusion of navigation/steering electronics from that list is a reasoned reading requiring qualified confirmation.

evidence.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (EUR-Lex summary)
evidence.supportedAssertion: Regulation (EU) 2025/40 (packaging and packaging waste, summarised as applicable 'from 2026') sets sustainability and labelling requirements for packaging throughout its life cycle, covers all packaging regardless of material or origin, and harmonises national measures. Producers are responsible for the entire life cycle including waste management through extended producer responsibility covering collection, sorting and recycling costs with modulated fees. Manufacturers and importers must conduct or ensure conformity assessment and keep technical documentation for five years (ten for reusable packaging), manufacturers must issue an EU declaration of conformity, ensure labelling, and take corrective action; distributors must verify compliance. It amends Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904 and repeals Directive 94/62/EC.
evidence.limitations: EUR-Lex summary; the entry-into-force and application dates were not rendered in the retrieved copy. The 12 August 2026 application date used in D23 is therefore flagged for qualified confirmation and is not presented as verified.

evidence.publisher: Diário da República (Portugal) — Decreto-Lei n.º 57/2017, de 9 de junho
evidence.supportedAssertion: Portuguese Decreto-Lei n.º 57/2017 of 9 June 2017 transposes Directive 2014/53/EU (RED) into Portuguese law and establishes the regime for making radio equipment available on the market, putting it into service and using it. Article 2(1) excludes equipment listed in Annex I and radio equipment used exclusively for public security, defence, State security and criminal-investigation activities; Article 2(2) provides that radio equipment covered by this decree-law is not subject to Decreto-Lei n.º 31/2017 (the EMC transposition) except for Article 4(1)(a); Annex I point 2 lists marine equipment covered by Decreto-Lei n.º 167/99 (the Portuguese marine equipment regime implementing the international conventions). Article 4 sets out essential requirements (health/safety, EMC, efficient spectrum use, plus delegated-act categories under Article 4(3)(a)–(i)). Article 11(1) lists manufacturer duties including technical documentation, conformity assessment, EU declaration of conformity and CE marking, retention of technical documentation and DoC for 10 years, serial/lot identification, name and postal address on the equipment or packaging, instructions and safety information in Portuguese, information on frequency bands and maximum RF power, a copy of the DoC with every unit, and identification of Member States with restrictions. Article 11(2) treats importers/distributors as manufacturers where they market under their own name/brand or modify the equipment. Article 12 limits what may be mandated to an authorised representative (the Article 11(1)(a)–(e) duties may not). Article 13 sets importer duties including Portuguese-language instructions. Article 17 refers to conformity assessment under Annex II (Module A internal production control), Annex III (Modules B+C) and Annex IV (Module H). Annex V lists the content of the technical documentation (a–i), Annex VI the content of the EU declaration of conformity, Annex VII the simplified EU declaration of conformity, and Annex VIII the charges for verification tests.
evidence.limitations: This is national implementing law, not the directive text, and it is used here as a faithful indicator of the RED requirement structure, not as a substitute for the directive. Portugal's Annex I marine-equipment exclusion is a national transposition feature and does not by itself settle the EU-level MED/RED boundary for any MAREA configuration.

evidence.publisher: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (Spain) — Registro de Productores de Producto
evidence.supportedAssertion: Spain operates a Registro de Productores de Producto (RPP) for producers subject to extended producer responsibility. The registration number that must appear on invoices of affected products is the code assigned by the RPP at registration, in the format SEC/AÑO REGISTRO/XXXXXXXXX, where SEC is the registry section (the page names 'ENV', 'NEU', 'SFT' and 'BOL'). The annual product information reporting window for products placed on the Spanish market in 2025 was open from 2 January 2026 to 2 April 2026 inclusive.
evidence.limitations: Spanish ministry page. It documents the packaging (ENV) extended-producer-responsibility registry and the reporting calendar; it does NOT document WEEE producer registration, battery producer registration or RoHS enforcement, which are separate instruments not retrieved this session.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA states that 'all products that read and or transmit NMEA 2000 information must be certified by NMEA'. The NMEA 2000 standard is a copyrighted work under a licence agreement; the standard is licensed by industry group and is not sold via an online store. The current published version named on the page is NMEA 2000 Version 3.000 (with amendments). Updates are provided at no cost to marine manufacturer members only, in good standing for the calendar year; non-members may purchase updates. Product certification is performed via the NMEA 2000 Certification Tool, which generates a mandatory encrypted certification file sent to NMEA for validation; only after validation is certification granted, and only then may the official NMEA 2000 logo and the term 'NMEA 2000 Certified' be used on marketing material. Each manufacturer must purchase an NMEA 2000 Manufacturer Code (assignment takes up to 60 days) and, for each certified product, a unique Product Code; each certified product must broadcast its class and function code. NMEA does not issue memberships to non-marine entities, and associate memberships do not qualify for the member discount on standard licensing fees.
evidence.limitations: The page's licensing-fee table did not render in the retrieved copy, so NO NMEA 2000 fee is asserted (UNKNOWN). The page does not state a certification timetable beyond the 60-day manufacturer-code assignment.

The current version named is NMEA 0183 Version 4.30 (December 2023), which replaced Version 4.11 (2018), with NMEA 0183-HS (38.4 kbaud) included as an appendix; the base bus is 4800 baud. Published price tiers: NMEA 0183 manufacturer-member price USD 1,150; government/industrial/testing USD 7,500; consumer electronics USD 10,000. NMEA 0183 manufacturer mnemonic codes carry an administrative fee of USD 200 and require purchase of the standard at the applicable industry-group price; codes are issued to companies, not individuals.
evidence.limitations: The page states no NMEA 0183 product-certification programme (unlike NMEA 2000); its absence on the page is recorded as 'not evidenced', not as 'no programme exists'. Prices are published schedules, not MAREA quotations, and are asserted as BUDGETARY_INDICATION only.

evidence.supportedAssertion: NMEA describes itself as a worldwide, member-based trade organisation revolving around marine electronics interface standards, marine electronics installer training, and an annual marine electronics conference and expo, with four main offerings and installer trainings/certifications recognised by manufacturers for installation, support and warranty. The NMEA registered address is 846 Ritchie Highway, Suite L4, Severna Park, MD 21146, USA, and the page is marked 'Copyright 2026 National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA)'.

The Portuguese producer-registration pages requested on 2026-11-02 (https://apambiente.pt/en/node/861 and https://apambiente.pt/residuos/registo-de-produtores-de-produtos) timed out through the retrieval endpoint and their content was NOT read. Article 14(5) defines a severe incident as one that negatively affects or is capable of negatively affecting the product's ability to protect availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of sensitive or important data or functions, or that has led or could lead to the introduction or execution of malicious code. evidence.supportedAssertion: Toradex documents production programming of secure boot for Torizon OS based modules: secure boot is configured by programming one-time-programmable e-fuses with the public key information of the signing PKI tree (8 fuse values for HAB, 16 for AHAB) and then, as the last step, setting a closing fuse; once the closing fuse is blown the SoC does not load an image not signed with the correct PKI tree and the operation cannot be reversed. Automatic fusing on first boot requires a Torizon OS image of at least version 7.2.0 with at least the Basic Chain of Trust configured and TorizonCore Builder of at least version 3.13.0 (3.17.0 for the build-command approach). The documented fusing logic avoids closing the device if fuse programming errors or HAB/AHAB events are reported. In-field fusing uses Torizon Cloud and requires a commercial licence for the Torizon Cloud account.
evidence.limitations: Vendor documentation for one SOM family and one OS/BSP path (Torizon OS and Yocto). It documents the mechanism and its irreversibility, not a MAREA design, key hierarchy, HSM choice, manufacturing station or test. It does not state which modules support which fuse-programming options; that matrix is referenced but was not retrieved. No MAREA image, PKI tree or product exists.
